summary: The change does what was asked. When the baseline looks up main's tip run and finds it in progress, it now reads that run every 20 s, up to the existing ci_wait_s, and reuses it if it passes. If the run fails, is missing, or is still running when the wait runs out, the baseline runs locally as before. It works by passing budget.ci_wait_s into green_run, but only for the main-tip lookup. The old RunsOnly wrapper is replaced by WaitsWhileRunning, which ends the wait on the first read if no run exists, so a missing run does not hold the baseline for the whole bound. The landed-candidate lookup still makes a single read. I read read_ci, Paced and with_ci_source_on to confirm the logic. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core baseline` in this snapshot: all 16 matching tests passed, the 4 new ones and the 5 existing ones included. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. Athena's "fails without the fix" runs show the criterion 1 and 2 tests fail when the fix is reverted. The planned run for criterion 3 used a malformed command (two test names in one cargo filter), so it proved nothing. By reading the test instead, its read-count assertion would fail without the fix (1 read instead of 76). The diff touches only the three planned files. One minor issue: doc comments in ci_result.rs and routing.rs still say the baseline makes one read with no wait. Those files are out of scope, and the CHANGELOG says so.
